failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor estimated the external load from only the last sample, so under oscillatory feed/split/combined disturbances the predicted upper levels and pump voltages oscillated, causing excessive setpoint travel, production error, and h2 band or upper-level limit violations. The worst scenarios were sine disturbances (dev_feed_sine_2, dev_feed_sine_1, dev_combined_sine_1).
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If step scenarios degrade, reduce the filter time constant or add a level-slope term to the load estimate so transients do not contaminate the filter.

self_check: The new load estimate is an exponential moving average over the window with time constant 120 s, and samples within 60 s of a setpoint or target change are skipped so transients do not corrupt it. Under a sustained step this filter converges within a few minutes, shifting the split as needed to relieve upper levels or pump saturation; under a zero-mean oscillation it attenuates the load estimate, keeping setpoints near the nominal constant-Q operating point and preventing the churn that caused band and upper-level violations. Production stays on target because every chosen setpoint pair lies on the constant-Q curve; smoothing the choice only reduces loop tracking error.
proposed_change: Replaced the instantaneous steady-state load estimate d1,d2 with an exponentially filtered estimate (time constant 120 s) that skips samples within 60 s of a setpoint or target change, so the supervisor responds only to sustained offsets and not to zero-mean oscillations.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor estimates the feed offsets d1/d2 from the single last sample, so a zero-mean oscillatory feed (sine) makes the estimate swing every call. Because Q at steady state is fixed by the setpoints, each setpoint swing itself injects production error and h2-band excursions that the PI loops cannot catch up with in 1.5-2 min, producing large |Q-target| integrals, h2-band seconds and setpoint travel in every sine scenario.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the instantaneous residual estimate with a long-window average of the mass-balance residual so zero-mean oscillations cancel, then re-check whether a shorter window or an exponential filter is needed so sustained step/ramp offsets are still caught fast enough.

self_check: The feed-disturbance estimate d1/d2 is now the mean of the mass-balance residual over the last 300 one-second samples, so an oscillatory feed (period of a few minutes) largely cancels and the constant-Q setpoint split stays near its optimal instead of chasing the swing; since Q is fixed by the two setpoints, holding them still keeps production on target. Sustained offsets (step/ramp) still accumulate in the average, so the existing constraint-bias term can shift production between tank1 and tank2 when an upper level approaches its limit or a pump approaches 12 V, using the model-based cost that already penalizes h3/h4 near the limit and v1/v2 near saturation.
proposed_change: Replace the single-sample feed-offset estimate with a 300-sample windowed average of the mass-balance residual so zero-mean oscillatory feed disturbances cancel instead of being tracked.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The worst scenarios are all oscillatory (feed/combined/split sine). The supervisor estimates the tank feed residual d1,d2 from the LAST sample only, so the estimate carries the phase of the oscillation. It re-solves the split every call and chases the swinging residual, moving the setpoints back and forth, letting Q swing far off target and driving h2 out of band and h3/h4 toward the upper limit (feed_sine_2: 272 s in-band, 123 s upper-level, 1.11 m travel; combined_sine_1: h3 reaches 0.85 m).
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: The new window-averaged feed residual should be validated against the step/ramp scenarios; if step compensation is now too sluggish, reduce the averaging window from the full 600 samples to a trailing 300 s to trade sine rejection against step response.

self_check: The steady-state feed residual d1,d2 is now averaged over the whole 600-sample window, so a zero-mean sinusoidal draw-off averages to nearly zero and the supervisor no longer chases its phase, while a sustained step keeps a non-zero mean and is still compensated. Because the chosen h1/h2 pair stays on the constant-Q curve (Q = a1*sqrt(2g*h1)+a2*sqrt(2g*h2)), production stays on target as the split moves, and the constrained search biases the split away from whichever upper tank would exceed ulim or whichever pump would exceed 12 V, with a 0.06 m/call slew limit so travel stays small.
proposed_change: Replace the last-sample steady-state feed residual (d1,d2) with its mean over the entire 600-sample telemetry window, so zero-mean oscillatory disturbances are filtered out and only sustained offsets move the setpoint pair.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Oscillatory feed disturbances cause the supervisor to chase a steady-state mass-balance residual that is corrupted by the tanks' level dynamics, producing setpoint churn, pump saturation, production off target, and upper-level violations.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Test whether including level slopes in the mass-balance residual improves both oscillatory and step responses without increasing setpoint travel.

self_check: The change recomputes the feed offsets d1,d2 using the full mass balance including measured level slopes, so transient level changes no longer masquerade as sustained feed disturbances. This gives a truer load estimate during setpoint moves and oscillations, reducing overshoot and pump saturation. When an upper level approaches its limit, the optimizer still biases along the constant-Q curve (adjusting the h1/h2 split) to keep h3/h4 safe, and the slew limiter prevents large single-step setpoint jumps.
proposed_change: Include the measured level slopes in the mass-balance residual when estimating the feed offsets d1 and d2.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor ignored dh1/dt and dh2/dt in the mass-balance feed-offset estimate, so during feed/split oscillations the estimated d1,d2 lagged the true disturbance by about 90 degrees; the setpoint bias was applied out of phase, causing large production deviation and h2-band/upper-level violations.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Proceed with the slope-corrected estimate and verify on oscillatory and step scenarios; if churn increases, add a reversal-only rate limiter as a follow-up.

self_check: The slope-corrected mass balance gives an unbiased instantaneous feed offset, so the supervisor's model-predictive step knows the true d1,d2 even while levels are moving. It then chooses the h1/h2 split along the constant-Q curve that keeps the predicted upper levels below their limits and the pump voltages within saturation; because the split always satisfies h1+h2 production, Q stays on target. The existing hold during its own setpoint transient prevents the slope term from reacting to control-induced level motion.
proposed_change: Include the measured h1 and h2 level derivatives in the mass-balance calculation of the feed offsets d1 and d2, so the disturbance estimate is not phase-lagged during oscillations.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The worst scenarios are sine feed and combined sine, where the supervisor chases the oscillatory feed residual. The instantaneous steady-state d1/d2 estimate ignores lower-tank level slopes, so during ramps it misreads pump-induced level changes as external feed; at dev_feed_sine_2 it raised h1 to 0.403, drove pump2 to 12 V, and pushed h3 above 0.75 m while Q stayed 0.5-1.5 L/s low. Similar behavior on dev_combined_sine_1 caused h3 and h4 limit violations and band excursions.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use the slope-corrected mass-balance residual for d1,d2 and re-evaluate upper-level headroom; then tune the hold time or add a short predictor if sine tracking still lags.

self_check: The supervisor estimates the instantaneous feed imbalance from the lower-tank mass balance, including the measured level slope, so the predicted pump flows Q1/Q2 stay valid during ramps and oscillations. It then searches the constant-production split for the point that keeps h3 and h4 below the limit and both pump voltages below saturation, with penalties for limit violations and setpoint motion. A 0.06 m step limit and a 45 s hold after its own setpoint changes keep the PI loops from chasing transients, so production stays on target while constraints are respected.
proposed_change: Add lower-tank level derivatives to the feed-disturbance estimate so d1,d2 reflect the instantaneous mass imbalance rather than the steady-state residual.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The worst scenarios are all sinusoidal feed/combined oscillations (dev_feed_sine_2 = 1659, dev_feed_sine_1 = 872, dev_combined_sine_1 = 872). The supervisor estimates the feed offsets d1 and d2 from the single last sample, so during a zero-mean oscillation the estimate swings in phase with the disturbance. It then moves the h1/h2 setpoints back and forth every call (up to 1.1 m of travel on feed_sine_2), which forces the slow PI loops to fight both the disturbance and a moving setpoint, enlarging the production excursion (758 L off target) instead of reducing it. The earlier rollbacks added level-slope terms to the same instantaneous residual and simply amplified this churn.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Filter the estimated feed loads over a full telemetry window before using them in the steady-state optimization so zero-mean oscillations produce no setpoint motion, while sustained steps/ramps still bias the split along the constant-production curve.

self_check: The supervisor averages the lower-tank mass-balance residual over the whole 600 s telemetry window, so a zero-mean oscillatory feed cancels out and the setpoints stay put, letting the PI loops absorb the swing while production stays near target. When the windowed residual does show a sustained bias, the model predicts the resulting h3 and h4 and the required pump voltages, and the split is re-optimised along the constant-production curve, biasing production toward whichever tank keeps the upper levels and the pumps inside their limits. Because setpoints only move for sustained offsets, the 45 s post-change hold and the 0.06 m per-call step cap keep total setpoint travel small.
proposed_change: Replace the single-sample feed-load estimates d1/d2 with their average over the entire 600 s telemetry window, so zero-mean oscillations cancel and only sustained load shifts move the setpoints.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Oscillatory feed and combined sine scenarios score worst because the supervisor uses the instantaneous mass-balance residual d1,d2; the setpoints then chase the zero-mean disturbance out of phase, producing large production offsets and h2/upper-level violations.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Validate the filtered load estimate on all sine and step scenarios; if step response slows too much, add a step detector to bypass the filter during sustained offsets.

self_check: The supervisor estimates feed/pump/split loads from the upper-level mass balances and averages them exponentially over a 60 s window, so a zero-mean oscillatory disturbance does not cause the setpoints to chase the oscillation out of phase. When a sustained load pushes h3 or h4 toward 0.75 m, the filtered estimate still rises and the cost function biases the h1/h2 split along the constant-Q curve to reduce the affected upper level. Pump-voltage saturation is handled in the same cost by penalizing predicted v1 or v2 above 12 V, so the chosen setpoints avoid demanding infeasible flows. Setpoint movement is rate-limited and transient samples after the supervisor's own changes are excluded, keeping travel small.
proposed_change: Replace the instantaneous feed-load estimate d1,d2 with an exponentially weighted average of the mass-balance residuals over the 10-minute window, excluding samples after the most recent setpoint change.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The worst scenarios are the oscillatory feed/combined-sine cases (dev_feed_sine_2=1659, dev_combined_sine_1=872). The supervisor computes its feed-offset estimate d1,d2 from the LAST sample only, so during a zero-mean oscillation the residual (and the setpoints chosen from it) swings back and forth with the disturbance. Because the PI loops lag the few-minute oscillation by 1.5-2 min, the resulting setpoint moves are out of phase, so production wanders, h2 leaves its band, upper levels cross the limit, and travel blows up to >1 m.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the single-sample feed-offset estimate with a time-weighted (exponentially filtered) average over the recent window so setpoints respond to sustained offsets, not the instantaneous oscillatory residual; leave the slope/derivative additions alone because those failed on pump_sine.

self_check: The supervisor now estimates the feed load d1,d2 as an exponentially weighted average over roughly the last 150 s of the window instead of the instantaneous residual, so a zero-mean feed/split oscillation largely cancels and the setpoints stop chasing it, cutting travel and out-of-phase production error. Sustained offsets still accumulate in the filter and are pushed into the constant-Q split before any upper level reaches its limit, where each candidate split is penalized for predicted h3/h4 overflow and pump saturation, keeping Q on target with the smallest feasible setpoint move.
proposed_change: Replace the single-sample feed-offset estimate with a 150 s exponentially-weighted average of the per-sample mass-balance residual, so zero-mean oscillations are smoothed out while sustained offsets still propagate to the constant-Q setpoint split.
